description: A whole Janus WebRTC session against /janus/ws, hand-recorded. The capture tool cannot reach any of this: Janus speaks neither HTTP nor the kvmd envelope here, half of what matters is a refusal, and the interesting messages arrive unprompted. Every SDP is scrubbed — addresses, DTLS fingerprints and ICE credentials are replaced with placeholders — and frame payloads are not stored at all.

steps.name: upgrade_unauthenticated
steps.description: No credentials. Janus never sees the request: kvmd's auth sits in front of it, so the refusal is the same envelope every other unauthenticated call gets, and there is no socket to read an error off.

steps.name: upgrade_without_subprotocol
steps.description: Authenticated, but the handshake does not ask for `janus-protocol`. Janus serves its WebSocket transport only under that subprotocol, so a client that does not name it gets no usable socket.

steps.name: upgrade
steps.description: The handshake that works: kvmd credentials plus the `janus-protocol` subprotocol, which the server echoes back. Nothing arrives until the client speaks first — unlike the kvmd event socket, Janus has nothing to say to a session that does not exist yet.

steps.name: create
steps.description: A Janus session. `data.id` is what every later message has to carry as `session_id`, and the session dies about sixty seconds after the last message unless something keeps sending `keepalive`.

steps.name: attach_unknown_plugin
steps.description: A plugin name Janus does not have. The error is Janus's own shape — `janus: "error"` with a numbered `error` object — and nothing like the kvmd envelope the rest of the API answers with.

steps.name: attach
steps.description: The ustreamer plugin, `janus.plugin.ustreamer`. `data.id` is the handle every plugin message has to carry as `handle_id`; a session can hold several.

steps.name: request_unknown
steps.description: A request name the plugin does not implement. It answers 405, and the error rides inside `plugindata.data` of a pushed event rather than at the top level — a plugin error is a successful Janus message.

steps.name: request_missing
steps.description: A body with no `request` at all: 400. Same place, same shape.

steps.name: request_not_a_string
steps.description: A `request` that is not a string: 400 again, with its own text.

steps.name: features
steps.description: What this build of ustreamer can do. `audio` and `mic` say whether the device has them wired up at all, and `ice` carries the STUN or TURN server kvmd was configured with — recorded as a marker here, because it can name a host that is not the device.

steps.name: watch
steps.description: The request that starts a negotiation. The ustreamer plugin is the offerer, so what it pushes back is `jsep.type == "offer"` and the client owes it an answer — the opposite way round from most WebRTC code. `result.status` is `started` even though nothing is flowing yet.

steps.name: trickle_completed
steps.description: This client gathers every candidate before it answers, so the answer above is already complete and the only trickle it has to send is the one that says so. Janus acknowledges a trickle and never events it.

steps.name: without_a_viewer
steps.description: The negotiation finished and no picture came. kvmd runs ustreamer only while a session asked to be counted as a viewer — `GET /api/ws?stream=1` — and the Janus plugin reads its frames out of ustreamer's memory sink, so with the streamer stopped there is simply nothing to send. Janus still completes the handshake and still says `webrtcup`: nothing in the signalling reports the silence.

steps.name: session_events
steps.description: Everything Janus sent on its own once a kvmd viewer socket was open beside this one and the streamer came back up. `webrtcup` means the DTLS handshake finished and media may flow; `media` is one per direction and kind, saying whether packets are actually arriving. None of these answer anything the client sent.

steps.name: frames
steps.description: Decoded video off the peer connection. Only the shape is recorded — the pixels are the attached host's screen, the same reason the media fixture stores frame lengths and nothing else.

steps.name: key_required
steps.description: Asks the encoder for a keyframe. The plugin sets a flag and says nothing further, so there is no push to wait for and a caller that waits for one waits forever.

steps.name: stop
steps.description: Ends the stream for this handle. The plugin answers `status: "stopped"`, and Janus tears the peer connection down behind it.

steps.name: after_stop
steps.description: What Janus sends once the peer connection is gone.

steps.name: keepalive
steps.description: What keeps the session from timing out. Janus answers `ack` and nothing else; the web UI sends one every twenty-five seconds.

steps.name: detach
steps.description: Drops the handle. The session stays.

steps.name: message_to_a_dead_handle
steps.description: The same message again, to the handle just detached. This is the top-level error shape — `janus: "error"` — as opposed to a plugin error, which arrives inside `plugindata` of a message Janus considers successful.

steps.name: destroy
steps.description: Ends the session. Every handle under it goes with it.

steps.name: keepalive_after_destroy
steps.description: A session id Janus no longer knows. Worth pinning because a keepalive loop that outlives its session sees this and nothing else — the socket stays open and healthy underneath it.
